Subject: SCCs — module preference and timeline

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our legal review we need to confirm which SCC modules Redwood intends to execute for EU→UK and EU→US transfers. Our counsel prefers Module 2 (Controller→Processor) for our relationship, but we've seen vendors offer Module 1 as a catch-all in some cases.

Could you please:
- Confirm Redwood's recommended module for Northstar Health (we are a data controller)
- Share the draft exhibit you referenced and any internal rationale for the choice (data flows, subprocessors, onward transfers)
- Provide an expected timeline for signed SCCs — procurement needs to lock this into our contract schedule

I've attached a redline of our DPA (attachment: northstar-dpa-redline.pdf) and the SCCs exhibit we received last week.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to finish by May 30.

Best,
Julia

Subject: Re: SCCs — module preference and timeline

Rachel — quick read and recommendation from Legal.

Summary recommendation: Recommend Module 2 (Controller→Processor) for Northstar Health. Rationale below:
- Relationship: Northstar is the controller; Redwood acts as processor for hosted API and Dedicated (we process on their behalf). Module 2 maps directly to that relationship and is what our counsel normally accepts for customer DPAs.
- Onward transfers: We may need optional Processor-to-Processor language for the US analytics provider; propose an enactment of Module 2 with a Processor Appendix that documents subprocessors and permitted onward transfers.
- EU→UK: Accept SCCs Module 2 + the UK Addendum (we will attach the UK addendum when executing for UK transfers).

Redlines / non-starters:
- We should not accept a customer-proposed Module 1 (Controller→Controller) because that mischaracterizes the processing role and can create liability.
- Avoid heavy data localization clauses and restrictions that block our standard backup and disaster recovery paths to GCP US; offer minimization and encryption compensations instead.

Timeline: Legal can turn an exhibit redline within 3 business days if we stick to Module 2 + Processor Appendix. If they insist on Module 1, we need commercial and Product signoff and that will add time.

Next steps for you:
1) Tell Northstar we recommend Module 2 and that we'll send a redlined exhibit by Tue, May 27.
2) Ask for confirmation of the US analytics vendor (so we can check subprocessors).

If helpful, I can draft the Processor Appendix template and loop in Compliance for evidence (SOC 2 scope).

— Marcus
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Julia — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. Brief update from our side:

1) Recommendation: Redwood recommends executing SCCs using Module 2 (Controller→Processor) for your account. This covers both our Hosted API and Dedicated offerings. For UK transfers we will attach the UK Addendum.

2) Onward transfers: We anticipate one US analytics subprocess (you can see it in the attached processor list). Legal proposes a Processor Appendix to document permitted onward transfers and security controls. If you can confirm the analytics vendor name and whether data shared is pseudonymized, we can finalize that section quickly.

3) Timeline: Marcus (Legal) will send a redlined SCCs exhibit + Processor Appendix by Tue, May 27. That should keep Procurement's May 30 target achievable.

Attachments: northstar-sccs-exhibit-draft.pdf, SCCs-module-comparison.xlsx

If you want us to switch to Module 1 we need a commercial and Product signoff and it will extend the timeline — happy to discuss tradeoffs on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Strategic Health
Redwood Inference
